passages.text: Omsom Ads Strategy: What Makes Omsom Ads Effective Omsom's advertising is built on cultural identity as brand substance, not marketing decoration. The Pham sisters' personal Vietnamese-American story, their pride in Asian food culture, and their frustration with inauthentic 'Asian-inspired' products drives every piece of content. Their collaborations with Asian-American chefs and the Chrissy Teigen partnership amplified reach while maintaining cultural authenticity. Browse Omsom ads on AdLibrary.

passages.text: Browse Omsom's ad creatives on AdLibrary at adlibrary.com. What platforms does Omsom advertise on? Omsom advertises primarily on Instagram and TikTok, with significant organic reach from the Pham sisters' personal content and community engagement. Who are Omsom's main competitors? Omsom competes with Fly By Jing, Momofuku Goods, and mainstream Asian sauce brands like Simply Asia and Thai Kitchen — though Omsom's cultural identity positioning is largely uncontested. What makes Omsom's ads effective? Omsom's ads work because cultural authenticity is impossible to fake — consumers can tell the difference between a brand that is Asian-American and one that is performing Asian-inspired.

passages.text: “Having lived a lifetime of being constrained by this model minority myth, we felt like embodying this noisy, loud, and proud energy was so true to us and is the way that we wanted to show up in the world through our company,” Vanessa says. passages.text: 1. Narrow your focus Vanessa believes many brands dilute their message when they try to appeal to everyone. Instead, she recommends narrowing your audience, which makes it easier to create more meaningful content. “We really centered the first- and second-generation Asian American community at a time where many brands were overlooking this audience,” Vanessa explains. Existing food brands often used either the same packaging as the products in Asia or they were aimed at non-Asian consumers with slogans like “travel the world through food.” Omsom means noisy or rambunctious in Vietnamese.

passages.text: 2. Make storytelling a daily habit “If you are not dedicating time and energy to storytelling, then the media doesn't have a story to tell,” Vanessa says. Omsom has made it a priority to create a daily habit around creating content, whether that’s sharing what’s going on behind the scenes or commenting on current events. That’s helped them develop good relationships with journalists and more impactful press coverage.

passages.text: About Omsom Omsom was founded in 2020 by sisters Vanessa and Kim Pham to create bold, authentic Asian starter sauces that make it easy to cook Asian meals at home without compromise. The brand's identity is explicitly Asian-American — the name means 'rambunctious' in Vietnamese — and their marketing embraces cultural pride as the primary brand driver.
